📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 on Friday, plunging through a major psychological price level as the selloff gathered pace after Anthropic’s stock market debut.

The daily chart reveals BTC at $59,703.72 , down 3.55% for the session after touching a low of $59,300.

The Fear and Greed Index chart dipped to 9, a reading classified as “extreme fear” and its lowest since February. For reference, the index was at 18 a week ago and a neutral 51 a month earlier.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

In a recent development, the indicator tracks crypto market sentiment on a scale from zero, or maximum fear, to 100, or extreme greed, using market data rather than individual investor surveys. Its 2026 low was 5 on February 5, compared with a yearly high of 82 on August 26.

In a recent development, the selling went well beyond Bitcoin. Ethereum fell 4.24%, Solana lost 6.36%, BNB slid 4.38% and XRP declined 5.53% over the same period.

Forced selling added to the pressure. As Decrypt reported earlier Friday, roughly $727 million in leveraged crypto positions had been liquidated over 24 hours, about 86% of them bullish bets, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $582.2 million on Thursday.

Spot fund withdrawals did not begin with Anthropic’s IPO. By Thursday, roughly $2.9 billion in U.S. Bitcoin ETF outflows for November, alongside higher Treasury yields and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut Thursday at $111.50, up 34% from the $83 IPO price, before closing at $97.17. Friday brought another decline for the Claude developer, with the stock almost losing all the prime it gained after its IPO.

The listing raised $81.34 billion through the public offering, but enthusiasm for Anthropic shares did not carry over to the companies building the AI boom.

In a recent development, friday’s market heatmap indicates tech stock suffering in the middle of mostly green pastures. Nvidia down 3.78%, Broadcom is down 5.65%, AMD declining 5.06% and memory-chip maker Micron dropping 6.51%. Meta fell 2.21%, adding to pressure on companies spending heavily on AI infrastructure.

Other major stocks were doing better. Alphabet rose 2.81%, Microsoft gained 0.50% and Apple edged up 0.25%, while healthcare stocks Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson rose 1.21% and 1.78%, respectively. Walmart added 2.91% and Visa climbed 1.34%.

But it was not a uniform crash across the S&P 500. The tech-heavy Nasdaq was falling more sharply than the broader index, while pockets of healthcare, consumer, and financial shares remained green.

According to recent reports, bitcoin’s daily chart turned more decisively bearish after the break below $60,000. Its 50-day exponential moving average, or EMA, was below the 200-day EMA, a death-cross configuration, and spot prices were trading beneath both lines. That confirms sustained downside momentum rather than a brief intraday dip.

In a recent development, the relative strength index, or RSI, had fallen into the teens, far below the 30 threshold usually associated with oversold conditions. The average directional index, or ADX, climbed to 43.7, signaling a strong trend, with the chart’s directional readings favoring sellers. Oversold does not mean a bounce is guaranteed.

The longer-range chart puts the $60,000 breakdown in context. Bitcoin traded around this area several times in 2024 and returned to it during the mid-2026 retreat, making it a visible historical price zone as well as a round-number threshold.

With $60,000 giving way, the roughly $58,000–$59,000 support area near the mid-2026 lows comes into focus. If that zone fails, the next notable historical demand area is around $55,000–$56,000, followed by the $50,000 region marked by the deeper 2024 selloff.

It has been revealed that for bulls, $60,000 is now the first level to hold. The next hurdle is $62,000–$62,500, followed by $65,000 and heavier resistance near $68,000–$70,000. A brief bounce back above $60,000 would not, by itself, reverse the bearish trend.

Industry observers note that as of right now, Bitcoin had touched $59,300.13, confirming that sellers had pushed below the $60,000 support zone. The next test is whether that level becomes resistance on a rebound.

The momentum adds fresh fuel to a bullish call from Jefferies, which just initiated coverage on SpaceX with a Buy rating and a $210 price target—implying roughly 64% upside from pre-rally levels.

In a research note titled It’s Just Rocket Science, Jefferies identified Starlink as the core engine behind SpaceX’s long-term valuation.

Jefferies projects Starlink could generate $92 billion in annual revenue by 2029—growing at a 70% compound annual rate—with operating margins exceeding 60%, according to Investing.com.

The core launch division is forecast to deliver $9 billion in revenue and $4 billion in EBITDA by 2029 as Starship scales toward 315 flights per year.

As hyperscalers race to secure electricity, data centers, and compute capacity, SpaceX’s orbital network and massive capital deployment position it to capture growing AI infrastructure demand.

It has been revealed that while Jefferies’ thesis originally framed SpaceX as a resilient play during the broader AI selloff, market sentiment flipped overnight. Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang just 11 days after his resignation—sending NVDA shares up roughly 30% and lifting the Nasdaq nearly 7%.

On Friday, the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped more than 10% below their record highs into correction territory, while the Nasdaq dropped roughly 5%, erasing its 2026 gains.

Nvidia sat at the epicenter of the rout, plunging roughly 13%–14% on Friday following CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation amid scrutiny over an alleged Chinese chip-smuggling link, alongside reports that SEC enforcement staff are reviewing potential accounting complications.

Newly public Anthropic also surrendered most of its first-day IPO gains during its second session, while expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike added pressure across high-growth tech.

For crypto traders, SpaceX’s stock trajectory matters on two fronts. First, high-beta tech and AI equities continue to dictate institutional risk appetite—sharp drawdowns in Nasdaq heavyweights often trigger short-term deleveraging across Bitcoin and AI-linked tokens.

Second, Jefferies’ thesis reinforces one of crypto’s strongest narratives: compute and bandwidth scarcity, a bottleneck driving capital toward both orbital infrastructure and decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePIN).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sui [SUI] crypto token is making headlines for various reasons, with the most notable being Hashi’s launch on the Sui mainnet, an attempt to make Bitcoin [BTC] more useful in decentralized finance (DeFi).

Earlier, Bitcoin holders had limited options when it comes to earning returns or accessing liquidity without selling their BTC. However, now with Hashi, there’s an option that allows owners to use their Bitcoin as collateral for loans and other financial products while retaining their exposure to BTC.

The process works through a token called hBTC. When a user deposits Bitcoin into Hashi, the protocol mints an equivalent amount of hBTC on the Sui blockchain at a 1:1 ratio.

To make the process even more seamless, Hashi uses Sui validators and a 2-of-2 multisignature setup to prevent any single entity from moving deposited Bitcoin independently. It also requires six Bitcoin network confirmations before issuing hBTC.

Its first major use case is lending through Fluid, where consumers can deposit hBTC as collateral and borrow USDC without selling their BTC. However, falling Bitcoin prices could trigger collateral liquidations.

Remarking on the same, Michaël van de Poppe, CIO & Founder at MN Fund, said,.

It’s one of the reasons why $SUI is my largest position in my Altcoin portfolio.

Besides this, the Sui crypto token has also made waves in the ETF ecosystem, wherein Grayscale’s Sui Staking ETF attracted $5.33 million in inflows during the week ending 20th November. Even as U.S. spot crypto ETFs collectively recorded $1.51 billion in net outflows.

In fact, its 19th November inflow of more than $5.43 million was reportedly its strongest single-day performance since its February launch.

That mentioned, Sui is also showing growth in its stablecoin ecosystem as its stablecoin supply increased by 7.36% to approximately $584.26 million.

In fact, according to a previous report by AMBCrypto, Sui’s stablecoin market cap outperformed the broader crypto stablecoin market, which contracted by around 5%.

Industry observers note that all these coincided with SUI trading at $0.6589 at press time, after a hike of 3.4% in the past 24 hours. Yet, despite the price hike, Open Interest has steadily declined to approximately $350-$400 million by late November.

This indicates that traders are closing their positions in SUI derivatives, pointing to a decline in speculative activity and leveraged exposure.

Industry observers note that david Schwartz, CTO Emeritus at Ripple and one of the creators of the XRP Ledger, has once again commented on his XRP and Bitcoin sales. This time, the reason was a viral post on X that claimed he had sold almost all of his crypto over the last few months.

According to the post, Schwartz's portfolio reportedly went from 26 million XRP, 1,500 BTC and 40,000 ETH to just 3 million XRP, 1 BTC and 6 ETH. The author called it "an insane reduction" and also referred to Schwartz as the current CTO of Ripple, while he now holds the emeritus title.

Schwartz replied that the timeline in the post was wrong. "That wasn't in the last few months, that was in the last decade," he wrote. As proof, he shared his own post from April 21, 2019. In that post, Schwartz noted he was still sticking to the "de-risking strategy" that he and his wife agreed on when they first decided to put their own money into crypto. He also admitted back then that selling during the bull run "still hurt.".

At the same time, Schwartz did not dispute the numbers themselves. "But it's basically true. I hate risk. I can't help it," he wrote in a follow-up post. According to him, pretty much every significant risk he has ever taken has worked out well, and rationally he should be taking more risk as he gets wealthier. "But I hate it. I just hate risk and can't do anything about it," Schwartz added.

It has been revealed that that wasn't in the last few months, that was in the last decade. You can find me talking about this in many posts over the years, like this one:https://t.co/5MgcPZ5qyG.

According to recent reports, at press time, XRP was trading at around $0.939, Bitcoin at $61,477 and Ethereum at $1,722. At these prices, the remaining 3 million XRP, 1 BTC and 6 ETH are worth about $2.89 million, and XRP accounts for more than 97% of this sum.

For comparison, at current prices, the peak holdings mentioned in the post would be worth over $185 million, with Bitcoin alone accounting for about half of it.

Recent findings suggest that schwartz has already explained his sales several times this year. In May, he said he did not have much XRP left and had tried to move most of his assets, other than Ripple stock, away from crypto exposure. In July, he said he regrets selling XRP at $0.10 and ETH at around $1, but noted that he and his wife had agreed to sell at every new all-time high.

Recent findings suggest that earlier in November, Schwartz disclosed that he sold about 2.5 million XRP in 2025. Per Schwartz, most of these tokens were received in 2020 and 2023, and he paid approximately $1.7 million in capital gains tax on those sales. He shared this in response to a user who called XRP a "terrible investment.".

In a recent development, among other things, Schwartz has previously noted that his main exposure to the crypto sector now comes through Ripple stock, not XRP. In March, Ripple rolled out a share buyback of up to $750 million that valued the company at $50 billion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia opened orders for two fresh PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK.

The PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business. Built on Hyundai Motor’s dedicated modular skateboard platform, E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to enable “limitless possibilities.”.

So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.

Kia added the PV5 Chassis, an open-bed model that can be converted into just about anything. In the UK, Kia is offering conversions through TGS Automotive Group, including lightweight tipper, Dropside, and Box solutions.

The PV5 Chassis is available exclusively with the long-range 71.2 kWh battery in the UK, which Kia noted could offer a potential WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km).

For reference, the PV5 Cargo L2/H1, which uses the same 71.2 kWh battery, offers a WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km). Other markets will also have a standard-range 51.1 kWh option.

The Chassis model is 4,610 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,935 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

Its compact size and 5.5-meter turning radius, Kia remarked, make it easy to maneuver in city streets, construction sites, and other tight work areas.

Inside, the PV5 Chassis features two seats. Like other variants, it includes a 12.9″ navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display with standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The Chassis model supports DC fast charging up to 120 kW, enabling the battery to charge from 10% to 80% in about 30 minutes. Using an 11 kW AC supply, it takes about 6 hours and 30 minutes to charge from 10% to 100%.

Industry observers note that payload depends on the configuration. Kia noted the Dropside offers a payload of up to 633 kg, while the Tipper can carry 561 kg.

In the UK, the PV5 Chassis is now on sale from £32,916 ($43,400) on the road, including the expected £5,000 ($6,700) UK Zero Emission Van Grant.

However, it’s an “incomplete vehicle,” as Kia describes it. The converted PV5 Dropside is priced from £40,110 ($53,500) on the road, including the ZEVG, while the PV5 Tipper starts at £41,310 ($55,000).

Industry observers note that kia also launched the larger PV5 Cargo L2/H2 in the UK. The new variant is 4,695mm long, 1,895mm wide, and 2,200mm high, with a 2,995mm wheelbase.

Industry observers note that the taller roof opens up an internal cargo-area height of 1,815mm. It also offers a greater load capacity than the L1/H1 and L2/H2, with 5.2 cubic meters.

It’s available in three- and four-door configurations with the choice of two or three seats. The three-door versions have a maximum payload of 630 kg, while the four-door models have dual sliding doors and offer a payload of up to 600 kg. Both versions can tow up to 1,500 kg.

Like the Chassis model, the PV5 Cargo L2/H2 is available in the UK exclusively with the 71.2 kWh battery, which provides a WLTP range of up to 239 miles.

Inside, it features the same setup as the other PV5 variants, including a 12.9″ touchscreen navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display.

The base PV5 Cargo L2/H2 Essential two-seat starts at £35,016 ($46,700), on the road, including ZEVG.

#156063. Tesla tuner Unplugged offers to take over Cybertruck production

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla tuner Unplugged offers to take over Cybertruck production

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive.
  • It comes just four days after Elon Musk stated Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.
  • UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The organization notes it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive. The organization publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors.

It comes just four days after Elon Musk stated Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.

UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The organization notes it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”.

In exchange, Tesla would collect a license fee plus FSD and Robotaxi network revenue on every vehicle built. UP even offered to let Cybercab get first call on battery cells. “We’ll wait our turn,” the tech giant wrote.

UP founder Ben Schaffer made it clear that he supports Tesla’s all-in move to autonomy, but he wants to keep the Cybertruck program alive.

It has been revealed that and it isn’t stopping at the pickup. UP notes it would build the Cybertruck, a three-row “CyberSUV,” and an unmanned “CyberCargo” hauler. Two vehicles Tesla has sometimes referenced, but they were never unveiled.

The post passed 240,000 views within hours, and the replies are mostly Cybertruck owners and Tesla shareholders begging Musk to say yes. Neither Musk nor Tesla had publicly responded at the time of writing.

UP has a lot riding on this. It sells an entire Cybertruck product line, the UP Invincible lift and armor kits, and it has scored several contracts to turn Cybertrucks into police vehicles for law enforcement agencies. CEO Ben Schaffer once described the tech giant’s purpose as doing “the things that Tesla maybe wants to do, but doesn’t have the bandwidth to do.” This is that idea taken to its extreme.

Sources indicate that musk framed the Cybertruck’s end as a space problem. He mentioned Tesla needs to “make room for increased Cybercab production.”.

In a recent development, if the Cybertruck program was successful, Tesla wouldn’t be killing it. Tesla also produces Model Ys at Giga Texas, and it is not shutting that down to make room for Cybercab.

As we reported when Tesla announced the wind-down, that explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of floor space, the Cybertruck line runs at about a quarter of its 125,000-unit installed capacity, and Texas had only a few hundred Cybercabs registered as of late October.

The real problem is buyers. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3, and we estimated 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks, a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. That was a good quarter by Cybertruck standards.

Industry observers note that even that number flatters it. S&P Global Mobility data highlighted SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, about 18% of US registrations that quarter. Tesla also tried a cheaper RWD trim, killed it, rolled out a $60,000 AWD version, then raised prices by $5,000 in August. None of it fixed demand.

Industry observers note that I’ll give UP credit for this: the offer calls Musk’s bluff. If the Cybertruck is really dying because Cybercab needs the room, here’s someone volunteering to take the line off Tesla’s plate. Problem solved.

Of course, it’s more complicated than that.

There are many ways this could fail or never happen in the first place, but there’s also a slight possibility that makes this possible.

First off, the backlash is real. If you look on social media and forums, yes, most of the discussion is about how Cybertruck is a failure, and Elon is lying about why Tesla is killing it, but there’s also a serious group of people, especially Cybertruck owners, who are genuinely upset that Tesla is killing the program because they love their trucks.

Most people have never driven a Cybertruck, but the steer-by-wire makes it a very addictive vehicle to drive, and even though the price is high, the value proposition for the specs is not bad compared to the very limited options for electric pickup trucks.

In other words, I wouldn’t necessarily bet against this effort, especially if they add an SUV variant and show the program some love with some tweaks here and there.

I could see a group of wealthy Cybertruck fans pooling money under Unplugged to make this happen, but getting Tesla to agree could be hard. It’s not unheard of for an automaker to sell a vehicle program to a dealer, like the Lotus Seven and Studebaker Avanti, but it would be a first at this scale.

It has been revealed that who is singing up to light their cash on fire? There is just no way that would work. Unless Tesla just gave them the designs and tooling. Then they are stuck the same problem with who is their market. There are 3 ev trucks coming that are cheaper better and more practical. Likey 3 or 4 more by the end of the decade.

You could make sense of it by looking at UP to Tesla as AMG to Mercedes. It’s not too massive a stretch, considering UP isn’t just your average Tesla tuner. It even worked with the automaker on its own version of the Model S Plaid.

If UP were to become for Tesla what AMG has become for Mercedes, it could make some sense for the firm to run a separate vehicle program that started under Tesla, but even as I write this, I realize that there’s very little chance this will happen.

But I wish them the best of luck, and I would be happy to see the Cybertruck live on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Big XRP Holders Add $72 Million While Supply Hardens.

Massive-time holders draw attention to XRP’s liquidity pockets sub-$1: is a bounce back signal getting delivered?

Large XRP holders have added roughly $72 million worth of tokens in recent days, even as major Bitcoin and Ethereum investors have reduced exposure during the broader market pullback.

The buying has coincided with a drop in available XRP on Binance, where reserves have reportedly fallen below levels last seen in July.

The move does not yet signal a clear bullish reversal. XRP was trading near $0.97, down about 3.6% over the previous week and still below its 200-day moving average near $1.26.

The combination of whale accumulation and thinner exchange balances has drawn attention to whether modest returning demand could produce a sharper price response.

An exchange supply-shortage measure for XRP rose to 2.4 on November 19, 2026 above its July reading of 2.09. Usually, readings above 2 are generally associated with unusually limited immediately available supply on the venue.

#XRP supply on Binance is getting tight. The Supply Shortage Index spiked above 8 in November and sits at 2.4 now, while price is still near $0.96.Supply is tightening and price has not responded yet. pic.twitter.com/xMTksTkKim.

Large wallets also pulled more than $127 million in XRP from Binance on a net basis between November 10 and 16, 2026.

Some of those movements may reflect internal exchange reserve management rather than pure investor withdrawals, particularly after operational disruption at the platform, so the flows are not a definitive accumulation signal on their own.

Lower balances can still matter if spot demand returns. Fewer tokens sitting on exchanges may reduce readily available selling pressure, especially if a portion of the withdrawn XRP is moving into longer-term storage rather than being repositioned for immediate trading elsewhere.

US spot XRP ETFs have gone 15 consecutive trading days without a net inflow, their longest dry spell since launch. Since their last positive day on October 29, the funds have recorded net withdrawals of about $26.3 million.

Industry observers note that total XRP ETF assets have fallen to roughly $1.08 billion from $1.77 billion in late September, though cumulative inflows since launch remain close to $1.78 billion. Existing holders have not abandoned the products in large numbers, but fresh capital has paused.

The divergence is the central feature of the current setup: large holders have been willing to buy into weakness, while ETF demand has stayed on the sidelines.

Tighter exchange supply could amplify a recovery if broader buying returns, but without renewed fund inflows and a reclaim of key technical levels, scarcity alone is unlikely to reverse the trend.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s possible to see a blockchain transfer within minutes, but that doesn’t mean a casino will process a withdrawal request that fast.
  • In a recent development, when reviewing a crypto casino in Canada, the first step should be to analyze the payment terms and ensure the casino is approved to take your business in your province.
  • Internal approval and blockchain processing are separate steps in a withdrawal request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s possible to see a blockchain transfer within minutes, but that doesn’t mean a casino will process a withdrawal request that fast. Various factors, including fees and the game being played, impact how promptly a withdrawal can be processed. With that in mind, readers should evaluate claims beyond the headline.

In a recent development, when reviewing a crypto casino in Canada, the first step should be to analyze the payment terms and ensure the casino is approved to take your business in your province. Just because a casino supports crypto payments doesn’t mean it’s licensed to take your business, offers instant payouts, or has games that have been vetted by an independent testing agency. Each of those should be supported by additional evidence.

Internal approval and blockchain processing are separate steps in a withdrawal request.

Look at each step of the withdrawal process in turn. Determine if a guaranteed timeframe covers the entire process or only certain requests.

A payment transaction hash is the best way to trace a payment. Prior to the payment being transmitted, account status or support can give information about the payment processing.

There are several costs associated with a crypto payment that should be taken into consideration. A wallet or exchange may charge a fee to send funds, a blockchain may charge a fee to process the transaction, and the casino may charge a withdrawal fee.

Recent findings suggest that conversion also needs to be considered. Deposits converted to a Canadian dollar balance need to consider exchange rates, conversion timing, and spread. Leaving funds in cryptocurrency means their Canadian dollar value can change, while the coin balance remains the same.

Sources indicate that look at minimum withdrawals and fees. A small payout can incur a high cost, especially with fixed fees. Promotions can also impact which funds are available for withdrawal.

Evaluate evidence supporting claims of game fairness. Consider how outcomes are determined and whether published rules are implemented. Look for game providers who are independently tested and named, rather than relying on a badge.

A stated return to player is based on the long-term average and does not prohibit large losses.

Some games offer “provably fair” verification. Note what the verification actually checks, and whether you can reproduce the check yourself. Verifying a specific outcome does not mean you can validate withdrawal reliability, the legality of the game, or the security of the components of the game.

According to recent reports, readers from Canada should check their local gambling authority. In Ontario, for example, iGaming Ontario has a directory of licensed operators, and OLG operates separately. Usually, the actual website is more key than recognizing the brand.

Industry observers note that look at account currency and payment totals to determine withdrawal terms. Keep a copy of the terms to show and explain discrepancies to support your case.

In a recent development, it’s key to assess speed of payout, fees, and fairness of a service separately. Assessing a service by the acceptance of cryptocurrency, in general, is a poor quality standard. It’s important to set limits on time and money spent, and to set funds apart, for example, for gambling, from funds that should be for saving or for daily expenses.

It’s that time again – Honda needs to roll out an electric Super Cub

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already.
  • According to recent reports, I’m not talking about an electric scooter vaguely inspired by the Super Cub.
  • In a recent development, the Honda Super Cub is arguably the most successful motor vehicle ever created, with well over 100 million produced since its introduction in 1958.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already.

According to recent reports, I’m not talking about an electric scooter vaguely inspired by the Super Cub. Not another futuristic concept with swoopy bodywork and a name that looks like a Wi-Fi password. I mean an actual honest-to-goodness Honda Super Cub, except electric.

The formula is already sitting right there.

In a recent development, the Honda Super Cub is arguably the most successful motor vehicle ever created, with well over 100 million produced since its introduction in 1958. It’s still in continuous production today.

In a recent development, and a huge part of that success comes down to how approachable the thing is. It isn’t supposed to be intimidating, excessively powerful, or particularly complicated. It’s simple, practical transportation wrapped in one of the most recognizable two-wheeler designs ever created.

In other words, it’s practically begging to become electric.

Industry observers note that the beauty of the bike is how simple and timeless it is, with the appearance barely changing in nearly 7 decades. And with the design freedom that electric drivetrains provide, upgrading the cute little bike to an electric future would be a walk in the park for Honda’s engineers.

An in-wheel motor would be a simple, cheap solution that frees up even more space in the body for batteries.

And Honda wouldn’t need some enormous battery capable of highway touring. Give an electric Super Cub enough battery for perhaps 50-60 miles (80-95 km) of real-world urban riding, a motor capable of roughly 50-60 mph (80-95 km/h), and simple Level 1 charging from a normal wall outlet. As a city runabout or a beachside cruiser, those middle-of-the-road specs would be perfect.

Industry observers note that even better, make the battery removable. Honda already has its Mobile Power Pack e: swappable battery system used in various electric two-wheelers, and an electric Super Cub would be an incredible platform to expand it.

The resulting bike could hit an unusually sweet spot.

There are millions of people riding electric bicycles today who will eventually want something faster, but don’t necessarily want a 500-pound (220 kg) electric motorcycle capable of hitting 120 mph (200 km/h). An electric Super Cub would be a natural next step: light, unintimidating, easy to ride, cheap to operate, and fast enough to actually function as a real urban vehicle.

It would also be one of the rare electric motorcycles that could appeal to people who aren’t necessarily looking for an “electric motorcycle.” An electric version is in such high demand that companies specialize in retrofit kits to convert classic Cubs into EVs.

Sources indicate that the Super Cub already has decades of cultural cachet. It’s cute. It’s useful. It’s nostalgic without feeling ancient. It’s the kind of motorcycle that can appeal equally to a lifelong rider and someone who has never considered owning a motorcycle before.

In a recent development, and perhaps most importantly, Honda could actually sell the thing globally. The same basic electric Super Cub could work in dense European cities, throughout Asia, and in American cities and suburbs. It doesn’t need to win spec-sheet battles. It just needs to be affordable, reliable, and unmistakably a Super Cub.

Recent findings suggest that my mum's old Honda-50 (the original cub, early 70's) had a tank that held less than a gallon of petrol. Range was realistically about 50 miles, but no-one even thought about that, it never ran out.

She traded for a honda-90, then a bunch of other stuff, I miss that 90, even now.

But the point is that range is not the concern, very few trips on these are more than 10 - 15 miles, say 30km round-trip.

But the real range, on a battery vehicle, is only about 2/3 of the claim,.

so if the claim is 80, it'll maybe do 55?

Thats enough, if it has the zip to handle traffic, and cruise at 45 - 50mph.

According to recent reports, honda has already shown that it understands the importance of electrifying small two-wheelers. It’s even made a token gesture with a Cub-like e-scooter in China. But there’s a difference between making another electric scooter and electrifying perhaps the most famous small motorcycle ever made.

So here I am once again, Honda.

Industry observers note that you’ve got the name. You’ve got the design. You’ve got the batteries. You’ve got the manufacturing scale.

Industry observers note that just put all the pieces together and give us the electric Super Cub already. The world is waiting, and will thank you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As demand for major crypto assets has increased, Ethereum remains on hold amid growing market fear and uncertainty, while exchange activities across the broad crypto market are showing a bearish trend.

While Ethereum remains one of the most affected cryptocurrencies during the prolonged crypto market volatility, the latest data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant indicates a massive slowdown in its exchange outflows.

Amid growing market fear, Ethereum outflows from Binance over the last month have hit a historic low as investors continue to move fewer ETH tokens away from the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

The data demonstrates that about 3.58 million ETH have been withdrawn from Binance over the last 30 days, marking an all-time low in Ethereum outflows on the exchange.

Further data reveals that the decline has come as Ethereum continues to struggle to stabilize its price and continues to weaken, trading around the $1,700 mark.

It is important to note that the decline in exchange outflows is expected, considering the growing market weakness and negative shift in investor sentiment over the period.

However, the metric has drawn different attention from market participants, given expectations that the massive security breach Binance suffered should trigger large withdrawals from the exchange.

Although blockchain trackers recently identified multiple large Ethereum withdrawals by the Binance hacker, it appears that the moves did not materialize into increased Ethereum outflows.

Apart from the attackers' withdrawals, it appears that Ethereum holders on the exchange did not respond to the attack in the conventional way, as security incidents like this often make investors more cautious and wary about keeping their assets on the exchange.

While this typically prompts them to transfer the assets into private wallets where they have greater control, it appears that Ethereum holders remained comfortable with keeping their funds on the exchange.

One rather unusual metric on XRP Ledger has seen more than a 3,062% increase in usage which raises a lot of questions. This is one of the largest spikes throughout the year in a function usage that mostly stays low.

Recent findings suggest that the function allows owners to manage their secondary keys for signing transactions on their wallets and/or accounts. Their main private keys stay offline, while a certain key issued by them is used in daily transactions.

It allows safer work and utilization of their wallets without potentially exposing their private keys. So even if someone grabs hold of your signing credentials, you'll be able to protect your funds by nullifying the issued keys, provided you still retain authorized access.

One way or another, the surge is bizarre. Most likely "legit" scenarios are: automated key rotations among large custodians like exchanges. Some security warnings that triggered massive migration and then, the illicit one: generation of function calls from bots or automated scripts.

Industry observers note that the flatlined chart actually represents tens or hundreds of calls daily, but a surge to nearly 4,000 is certainly out of the blue. Unfortunately, we were unable to identify the source of those transactions.

Recent findings suggest that the feature itself is legitimate, so the spike alone does not indicate that customers' funds or wallets are at risk. However, an undisclosed exploit or security problem cannot be ruled out without further investigation.

According to recent reports, one concerning scenario would involve malicious actors gaining access to wallets and assigning upcoming regular keys to maintain control over them. This would not necessarily mean that the XRP Ledger itself has been compromised, but rather that individual accounts may have been targeted.

For now, there is no evidence pointing toward such an attack, and the activity could just as easily be attributed to routine security operations.

Still, XRP holders should keep an eye on any unexpected changes to their account settings, especially regular keys they did not authorize.

It has been revealed that whether this was a coordinated security upgrade, automated activity, or something more concerning remains unclear. What is certain is that such an unusual spike deserves closer attention, particularly if similar activity continues over the coming days.

XRP has fallen below the $1 level even as available supply on Binance appears to be shrinking, leaving the token between constrained exchange inventory and a lack of fresh institutional buying.

According to recent reports, recent reports put XRP near $0.95 after a steep monthly decline, with the token briefly trading under $0.90 during November’s broader sell-off. Intermittent rebounds have occurred, but price has not yet established a durable hold above the $1 mark.

US spot XRP ETFs have gone through their longest stretch without a net inflow since launch, according to SoSoValue data. The funds last recorded an $8.43 million net inflow on October 29 and have since seen roughly $26 million in withdrawals, though flows on November 18 and 19 were described as flat rather than net negative.

The pause matters because ETF buyers had previously provided incremental demand. Total net assets in the funds stood at about $1.08 billion by November 19, down from roughly $1.77 billion in late September, while cumulative inflows since launch remained near $1.8 billion.

According to recent reports, XRP’s price action reflects that gap. The token was down about 3.6% over one recent seven-day period and roughly 28% over the prior month in another snapshot. Its 30-day Sharpe ratio was reported near negative 0.41, indicating that recent returns have not compensated for the asset’s volatility.

Sources indicate that cryptoQuant’s XRP Supply Shortage Index for Binance rose to 2.4 on November 19, above its July reading of 2.09. Readings above 2 are described as severe tightness, and net withdrawals from the exchange exceeded $127 million between November 10 and 16.

Lower exchange balances can reduce immediately available selling inventory, but they do not form a standalone bullish signal. One analyst noted that part of the movement could reflect internal Binance reserve management rather than accumulation by long-term holders.

It has been revealed that XRP’s price action has not yet confirmed stronger demand. XRP remains below its 200-day moving average, sitting very near $1.26, and repeated closes below $1 have turned that former support into nearby resistance.

Traders are watching the $0.94 area first, followed by support around $0.88. A sustained break below the latter could open a path toward $0.80, while a recovery would need to reclaim roughly $0.985 and then $1 before a broader reversal appears more credible.

Industry observers note that the more relevant signal for the market is whether ETF flows resume as Bitcoin and broader risk sentiment stabilize. Tighter supply can amplify a move higher, but without returning demand it can also coexist with a fragile price floor.

The macroeconomic calendar has several important data releases this week, with the October PCE Inflation report on Wednesday being the most significant. With only two weeks until the next FOMC meeting, these releases may have an impact on market expectations for the Fed’s next potential rate move. However, investor positioning already suggests that crypto assets remain vulnerable.

Investor Bill Ackman mentioned in a post on X that given increased spending on AI technologies and increased borrowing costs at SpaceX (now at 8.259%, compared to less than 6% pre-IPO), a 3% inflation target may be a more realistic target than 2% as set by the Federal Reserve.

In addition, Elon Musk also raised concerns around the increasing cost of components (chips, energy, data centers, etc.) in AI systems, and how this is putting pressure on firm balance sheets, reinforcing concerns that AI may cause prolonged inflationary pressures.

In this light, markets are still leaning towards the Fed holding rates at the upcoming FOMC meeting, even if October’s inflation data comes in hotter than expected. However, some investors believe rate hikes are already being priced in as a way to cool the AI boom and curb rising valuations.

Sources indicate that naturally, such uncertainty in Fed policy is putting more pressure on crypto markets. As such, given that risk appetite is also low, the question is whether a year-end crypto crash is becoming a bigger possibility.

It has been revealed that over the last 48 hours, the U.S. market has seen significant selling pressure.

Sources indicate that the sell-off has triggered a broad de-risking across equities, metals, and crypto, wiping out trillions in market value. U.S. equities alone have shed $5.5 trillion in market cap, while the crypto market has lost around $2.2 trillion. Bitcoin [BTC] slipped below $56k as selling pressure spread across the market.

Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump warned that things “will only get worse,” blaming Democratic midterm election wins for wiping out nearly $6 trillion in stock market value since the election. However, investors aren’t entirely buying this explanation. Instead, concerns around Fed policy, sticky inflation, and the rising U.S. debt ceiling are increasingly driving market fears.

The result? Some investors now see the possibility of further rate hikes as a “deliberate” move to cool an overheated market.

Sources indicate that this relates to the debate around the likely decision of the Fed. While some are concerned that further interest rate rises may cause a recession within the economy, others believe tighter monetary conditions are required to put inflated market values back into line.

In this scenario, the next two weeks could prove crucial for crypto markets. With AI bubble concerns building, major macro data ahead, Trump’s latest warning, and growing uncertainty around the Fed’s next move, crypto’s recent dip could be the start of a much broader correction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Long-time Shiba Inu community member and SHIB developer, Mazrael, has reacted to Solana-based memecoin platform Pump.fun's recent wallet login changes, which are sparking concerns about private key security.

In a new announcement, Pump.fun stated that external wallet sign-in is being retired on November 30, 2026. Starting November 30, 2026 (15:00 UTC), Pump.fun on the web will only allow users to sign in with an email account or a Google, Apple, or GitHub account instead of an external wallet such as Phantom, Solflare, or Ledger.

In a recent development, pump.fun reassures users that nothing will happen to their funds or account, as their wallet address, positions, callouts, followers and username remain unchanged. The only change is how users sign in.

Owners who sign in to their accounts with Phantom or any other wallet are urged to take action before the November 30, 2026 deadline.

According to recent reports, pump.fun outlined a number of steps for owners on how to switch their sign-in; of particular concern is the step that asked users to enter their wallet details and paste their private key when prompted. Pump.fun noted that this step encrypts the key in the user's browser and that the key is end-to-end encrypted by its login provider, Privy, allowing users' wallets to continue working for everything else.

Mazrael reacted to the development, drawing attention to the potential security implications for users.

pumpfun is retiring external wallet logins on web starting Nov 30. From then on you sign in with Google, Apple, email or GitHub. To keep your existing account..... they want you to paste your private key into their Privy flow 😬 Also note their own terms says they won’t ask for private keys...

The standard security practice across the cryptocurrency industry is that exchanges, wallet providers and other platforms do not ask users to disclose their private keys or recovery phrases. Such warnings are routinely issued to protect users from unauthorized access to their funds.

The Pump.fun wallet login change process appears to contradict this widely promoted security principle, Mazrael noted.

Private keys are highly sensitive credentials that give holders direct access to their cryptocurrency wallets. Whoever gets their hands on them might be able to access those wallets and move the funds. In general, it is recommended never to share private keys with individuals, support agents or third-party services.

#156044. Breaking: QuantumScape unveils Osprey all-solid-state cell: 1,000 cycles at 1 atm

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1598 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: QuantumScape unveils Osprey all-solid-state cell: 1,000 cycles at 1 atm

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • QuantumScape (QS) is finally going all-solid-state.
  • That’s a significant deal for the sulfide camp, which includes Toyota, Samsung SDI, BYD, and Factorial.
  • Here’s something QuantumScape has rarely spelled out this plainly: its current product isn’t all-solid-state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QuantumScape (QS) is finally going all-solid-state. Its latest Osprey platform swaps the liquid in its cathode for a sulfide solid electrolyte, and the firm says the cells have hit 1,000 full cycles to 80% capacity at just one atmosphere of pressure.

That’s a significant deal for the sulfide camp, which includes Toyota, Samsung SDI, BYD, and Factorial. Their cells typically need heavy clamping to work. But the white paper behind the announcement shows these are small, early lab cells, and some headline numbers come with important conditions.

Here’s something QuantumScape has rarely spelled out this plainly: its current product isn’t all-solid-state.

The latest white paper describes the QSE platform, including the QSE-5 cell it’s shipping as samples from its Eagle Line pilot production in San Jose, as a ceramic separator paired with “a relatively conventional high-nickel NMC cathode and a liquid catholyte.”.

Industry observers note that the solid part is the separator. It sits between the cathode and a lithium-metal anode that QuantumScape doesn’t manufacture at all. The cell is built “anode-free,” and lithium plates against the separator during the first charge.

Osprey keeps that separator and anode-free design and swaps the liquid in the cathode for a solid sulfide electrolyte. That makes the whole cell solid.

Industry observers note that the interesting part is that QuantumScape hasn’t changed its mind on sulfides. It has spent years arguing that sulfide electrolytes can’t work as separators, and the white paper doubles down, calling their problems “fundamental properties” of the material rather than engineering challenges.

The firm lists four issues: sulfides react with lithium metal, they need high pressure to keep contact with the electrodes, they struggle at room temperature and below, and they can’t handle fast charging with a lithium-metal anode before dendrites form.

Recent findings suggest that the pressure point is the one automakers care about most. QuantumScape illustrates it this way: 20 atm on a single 10 x 24.2 cm cell works out to roughly 5,000 kg of force, about three mid-size cars. Holding that across a pack takes thick steel end plates and tie rods, which add weight, volume, and cost.

According to recent reports, and 20 atm is on the generous side. Many sulfide cells in labs run at 30 to 100+ atm (3 to 12 MPa), and some even higher. China’s FAW reported large-format sulfide cells cycling at 5 MPa, or about 50 atm, in September, which was billed as a low-pressure achievement.

So QS’s pitch is simple: keep the sulfide in the cathode, where it’s good at moving lithium ions, and let the QS ceramic separator handle the lithium metal.

QuantumScape published four main data sets:.

Sources indicate that this is the strongest result. A 2-layer cell with a 50 x 65 mm cathode, the same area as QSE-5, ran 1,000 cycles to about 80% capacity. The test used full 1C charge and 1C discharge, 0 to 100% state of charge, 30°C, and 1 atm. The cathode loading was 5.5 mAh/cm², which is in line with commercial EV cells.

QuantumScape says no other sulfide-based cell has shown this, and Electrek couldn’t find published data that contradicts it. Academic groups have shown sulfide cells running with little or no external pressure, but not for 1,000 full cycles with a sulfide cathode and lithium-metal anode.

But this is a small cell. By our math, two layers at that size come out to roughly 0.3 to 0.4 Ah, compared to about 5 Ah for a QSE-5.

Sources indicate that the press release claims “five-minute fast charging from 10% to 80%.” The white paper highlights that was achieved at 10C, in a 2-layer cell, at 80°C (176°F). The chart itself is captioned “High temperature enables 5 min fast charge.”.

Sources indicate that batteries charge much faster when hot, and EVs do precondition packs before fast charging. Still, 80°C is well above what EV packs are usually preconditioned to before a fast charge. QS didn’t publish a room-temperature fast-charge result.

“Operational down to -20°C” came from a single-layer cell with a 21 x 21 mm cathode, discharged slowly at C/3. It kept 68% of its room-temperature capacity at -20°C (about 52% of its energy) and 85% at 0°C.

It has been revealed that that’s a real result for a sulfide system, which have historically needed heat. But it’s a tiny cell at a gentle rate.

Industry observers note that the “up to ~1,100 Wh/L” figure is a projection. QS notes high-loading cathodes (10 mAh/cm², about double today’s EV cells) are possible with sulfide catholytes. The test backing that up used an 11 mm coin-size cell at 3 atm, not 1 atm, and ran for 100 cycles.

For reference, QSE-5 is rated at 844 Wh/L and 301 Wh/kg.

The business model is the bigger story.

Recent findings suggest that quantumScape is pitching Osprey as an “open platform.” Customers can use QS’s own sulfide cathode, made with a proprietary dry process, or bring their own. QS states it has already tested Osprey with solid cathodes developed by its automotive customers.

In other words, after years of being the sulfide skeptic, QuantumScape now wants to sell its separator and anode-free design to the companies that have spent billions developing sulfide cathodes.

According to recent reports, that fits the licensing model it already uses with Volkswagen’s PowerCo and Honda. QS reported $9.8 million in customer billings in Q3 and declared a 100 MWh production line targeting start of production in 2028 for QSE-5.

According to recent reports, there’s no timeline for Osprey. The white paper notes the process has been demonstrated “at laboratory scale,” that higher-throughput processes are “in the development stage,” and that “significant work remains in process engineering.” Automakers also want larger prismatic cells than QSE-5, which means more layers and more area per layer.

It has been revealed that everyone else is on the clock. Samsung SDI is targeting mass production of sulfide all-solid-state cells in its Ulsan plant in the second half of 2027. BYD looks small-batch sulfide solid-state production in 2027, with mass production toward the end of the decade. Toyota is aiming for 2027 to 2028, after slipping from 2020, 2023, and 2026. Factorial’s sulfide Solstice platform is targeting up to 450 Wh/kg.

CATL, the world’s largest battery maker, said in June that true mass-market solid-state is still “years away,” around 2030.

None of those companies has published 1,000-cycle data at 1 atm with a sulfide cathode and lithium-metal anode. That’s QuantumScape’s opening shot.

It has been revealed that this is the most interesting thing QuantumScape has published in a while. The numbers are good, but the strategy shift probably stands out most.

According to recent reports, the cycle-life result is legit. A 2-layer cell with commercial-area electrodes and realistic loading doing 1,000 full 1C cycles at 1 atm and 30°C is the kind of data the industry hasn’t shown. And QS published the test conditions, which is more than many of its competitors do.

Key thing to remember is that this is a lab test cell. There's a long road ahead to mass manufacturing.

Industry observers note that also, when it hopefully hits the market it will be an incremental improvement, not a quantum leap. Current cells are already in the market doing things like 5 minute charging.

In a recent development, but you can argue the press release oversells what’s in the white paper. A 5-minute charge at 80°C isn’t the same thing as a 5-minute charge, and the release should have said so. The energy density is projected, the cold-weather result is from a cell the size of a postage stamp, and 80% after 1,000 cycles is well below the 95% after 1,000 cycles PowerCo confirmed in QSE’s early cells back in 2024. Different chemistry, different stage, but something worth keeping in mind.

According to recent reports, so QuantumScape is essentially admitting the liquid catholyte in QSE isn’t the end game, and that the industry’s massive sulfide investment is something to plug into rather than fight. If your separator is the one part everyone else can’t make work, selling it to them is smart.

The question is time. QS is still scaling QSE-5, with a 100 MWh line not due until 2028. Osprey is a lab process. Will anyone in the sulfide camp license it before their own 2027 to 2030 production aims lock in? At this point, it sounds like this is QS’ bet right now.

Sources indicate that if you’re following battery breakthroughs because you want cheaper, cleaner energy at home, the tech that already works is solar plus storage. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Risk appetite returned in force on Monday—but big players aren’t acting like the bottom is in.
  • Bitcoin price climbed approximately 4% to around $63,200 on November 23, staging a sharp recovery after plunging to a Saturday low of $55,081 over the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Hits $63K on Nvidia News—Could It Be a Trap?

Risk appetite returned in force on Monday—but big players aren’t acting like the bottom is in.

Bitcoin price climbed approximately 4% to around $63,200 on November 23, staging a sharp recovery after plunging to a Saturday low of $55,081 over the weekend.

It has been revealed that the rebound followed a sudden turnaround in U.S. tech equities and a wave of forced liquidations across crypto derivatives markets.

US markets staged a sharp rebound on Monday, November 23, led by a stunning 26% surge in Nvidia (NVDA) shares, after the firm’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director.Read the release: https://t.co/x4bnjiSVil.

The move helped reverse the recent tech and AI sell-off, sending Nasdaq 100 futures up 3.1% and S&P 500 futures up 2.4%, lifting risk appetite across global markets, including crypto.

In a recent development, bitcoin price recovery was further amplified by a short squeeze. More than $440 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including $370.2 million in shorts. Bitcoin short liquidations alone accounted for $172.91 million, according to CoinGlass.

Sources indicate that despite Monday’s bounce, underlying institutional data reveals ongoing caution. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $669.16 million in net outflows on Friday—their largest single-day capital exit since June 25, according to SoSoValue.

Over the past week, spot Bitcoin ETFs lost roughly $1.8 billion, marking their fourth consecutive week of net outflows.

Industry observers note that corporate accumulation also indicated signs of restraint. Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, purchased 457 BTC for $28 million last week—a modest addition compared to the $212 million it spent repurchasing its own STRC stock over the same period.

“The biggest Bitcoin corporate holder isn’t capitalizing on the dip,” crypto investor Ted Pillows noted on X.

Market analysts remain divided on whether the weekend drop marked a final floor or a temporary pause before another leg down.

Prominent trader Astronomer (@Astronomer_zero) suggested on X that while Bitcoin approached a macro bottom near the $56,000 level over the weekend, the current move to $63,200 is likely a relief bounce rather than a confirmed bottom, warning that a downward retrace remains probable.

$btc 56k bottom looking really good now, with a 10%+ bounce so far.Even though I think this will retrace and I deem it just a bounce, it is a very crucial bounce and a strong bounce like this has significance and is exactly what we wanted to see.If you remember my short… https://t.co/TzN9MxF9tc pic.twitter.com/WitozYCG5Z.

However, the trader argues that a durable bottom is forming soon and expects Bitcoin to hold above $50,000.

His thesis centers on Bitcoin’s estimated electricity production cost—presently around $60,300—which has historically served as a reliable long-term accumulation zone during cycles in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2026.

When prices dip below mining electricity costs, inefficient miners shut down, network difficulty adjusts downward, and supply pressure eases, establishing a technical and economic floor near $50,000.
